title: Innocent But Locked Up
summary: The court declared them acquitted and ordered release. Why did the prison keep them locked up until contempt was filed? Audits 1,000 SHA-256-pinned 2021–2026 official orders and oversight records across the Supreme Court, all 25 High Courts, 29 States & UTs, prison & police portals, NHRC/SHRCs, NALSA/SLSAs, Digital Sansad, Union Ministries, and CAG reports — verifying post-acquittal detention overruns, contempt actions, and subsequent releases alongside verified Cleared compliance benchmarks.
jurisdiction: India (Union of India & 29 States/UTs; All 26 Constitutional Courts)
authority: Supreme Court, 25 High Courts, State Prison & Police Depts, NHRC/SHRCs, NALSA/SLSAs, MHA, DoJ & CAG
statutory_anchors: Constitution of India Art. 21 (Protection of Life and Personal Liberty) & Art. 215 (High Court Contempt Power)
Contempt of Courts Act 1971 Sec. 2(b) & Sec. 12 (Wilful Disobedience of Judicial Release Orders)
Supreme Court FASTER Directives (In Re: Delay in Release of Convicts / SMW(Crl) No. 4/2021)
BNSS 2023 Sec. 479 (formerly CrPC Sec. 436A) & Model Prisons and Correctional Services Act 2023
Protection of Human Rights Act 1993 Sec. 12/18 & RTI Act 2005 Sec. 4(1)(b)/6(1)
scope: 1,000 live-verified, SHA-256-pinned 2021–2026 primary records spanning all 26 constitutional courts (Supreme Court + 25 High Courts) and all 8 official portal categories
Flagship Anchor Task #1 (p10-court-2024-anchor-bashir-ahmad-koka-v-chandraker-bh-0001): full 4-stage paired-PDF custody-overrun & contempt chain verified in downloaded court bytes
Includes 134 verified compliant/timely-release benchmark tasks published as Cleared with equal journalistic standing
out_of_scope: CAPTCHA-gated eCourts/ePrisons searches, login-walled portals, or dynamic non-byte-stable web pages
Private personal identifiers (Aadhaar, PAN, phone numbers, personal emails, bank details — scrubbed per DPDP Act 2023)
Accusatory or conclusory labels barred under BNS Sec. 356 fair-reporting standards
